gloss: smear, anoint; anointed one, Messiah; anointing oil
summary: To smear or rub a thing with oil or colour, and above all to anoint with oil: a pillar, the tabernacle and its altar, the priest, the king, and once a prophet, so setting them apart to Yahweh for his service. The one so set apart is מָשִׁיחַ, the anointed: the anointed priest, Saul and David and their sons as “the anointed of Yahweh”, Cyrus and the patriarchs whom Yahweh chose without any oil, and the anointed one of Psa 2 and Dan 9. The New Testament carries the word over as Μεσσίας, translated Χριστός, and names Jesus the anointed one, whom God anointed with holy spirit and power. The noun מִשְׁחָה is the anointing and its holy oil. Arabic masaḥa “wipe with the hand, anoint with oil”, Jewish Aramaic מְשַׁח and the Peshitta's ܡܫܚ “anoint” share the sense.

words.gloss: smear, rub with oil; anoint (to an office); be anointed
words.summary: About seventy times, in the qal and niphal. The act is smearing or rubbing on (wafers rubbed with oil, a house painted with vermilion, a shield oiled), and in most of its uses the pouring or smearing of holy oil on a thing or a man to set him apart to Yahweh: “he poured some of the oil of anointing on the head of Aaron and anointed him, to consecrate him” (Lev 8:12). Who anoints is the prophet or priest, the people or elders, and in the end Yahweh himself (“I anointed you king”, 2Sa 12:7).

stems.gloss: smear, rub, paint; anoint (a thing, a priest, a king, a prophet) with oil

senses.definition: To spread oil or paint over a surface with the hand: unleavened wafers rubbed with oil, a shield oiled for battle, a cedar house painted red, the body rubbed with fine oils.

evidence.note: Of the king's new house, panelled with cedar “וּמָשׁוֹחַ בַּשָּׁשַׁר”: painted with vermilion, the colour smeared on.
Cakes “mixed (בְּלוּלֹת) with oil” and wafers “מְשֻׁחִים with oil”: one kind kneaded in, the other rubbed over.
“Unleavened wafers anointed with oil.”
“Arise, princes, מִשְׁחוּ מָגֵן”: oil the shield for the battle.
The careless in Zion “drink wine from bowls, and anoint themselves with the first of the oils (רֵאשִׁית שְׁמָנִים יִמְשָׁחוּ), but are not grieved over the breaking of Joseph”.

senses.gloss: anoint (a pillar, the tabernacle, the altar), so as to make it holy
senses.definition: To put oil on a stone or on the tabernacle and its vessels and so set it apart to God; the anointing and the consecration go together.

evidence.note: “I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed (מָשַׁחְתָּ) a pillar”: the pillar on which Jacob poured oil (Gen 28:18).
“Take the oil of anointing and anoint the Dwelling and all that is in it, and consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.”
“Anoint the altar of burnt offering … and the altar shall be most holy.”
“With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony.”
“You shall anoint it to consecrate it.”
“Moses took the oil of anointing וַיִּמְשַׁח the Dwelling and all that was in it, and consecrated them.”
On the day the Dwelling was set up Moses “anointed it and consecrated it and all its vessels, and the altar”.
Among the ends of the seventy sevens: “to anoint a holy of holies (וְלִמְשֹׁחַ קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים)”.

senses.definition: To pour the holy oil on Aaron's head and sprinkle it on his sons, setting them apart to serve as priests; the high priest is “the priest whom one anoints in his father's place”.

evidence.note: “Take the oil of anointing and pour it on his head, and anoint him.”
“You shall anoint them and fill their hand and consecrate them, and they shall serve me as priests.”
“Anoint them as you anointed their father … and their anointing shall be to them an everlasting priesthood.”
“He poured some of the oil of anointing on Aaron's head, and anointed him, to consecrate him.”
“The priest whom he anoints and whose hand he fills to serve as priest in his father's place.”
“The sons of Aaron, the anointed priests (הַכֹּהֲנִים הַמְּשֻׁחִים).”
The manslayer stays in the city of refuge “until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil”.
“They anointed him to Yahweh as leader, and Zadok as priest.”

senses.definition: To pour oil on a man's head and so make him king or ruler (נָגִיד) at Yahweh's word; done by a prophet or priest, or by the people and elders, but owned by Yahweh as his own act.

evidence.note: “Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head … and said, Has not Yahweh anointed you ruler over his inheritance?”
“You shall anoint him ruler over my people Israel, and he shall save my people from the hand of the Philistines.”
“Arise, anoint him (מְשָׁחֵהוּ), for this is he.”
“Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and the spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day onward.”
“Yahweh sent me to anoint you king over his people.”
The men of Judah “anointed David king over the house of Judah”.
Nathan: “Thus says Yahweh … I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.”
“Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon.”
Elijah is sent to anoint Hazael king over Aram.
“Take the flask of oil and pour it on his head and say, Thus says Yahweh, I have anointed you king over Israel.”
Joash: “they made him king and anointed him, and clapped their hands and said, Let the king live!”
Jotham's fable: “The trees went out to anoint a king over them.”
David: “I am weak today, though anointed king.”
“I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.”
To the king: “You love righteousness and hate wickedness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions”, applied to the Son in Heb 1:9.

senses.gloss: anoint (a prophet); anoint with the spirit, to send
senses.definition: To appoint a prophet by anointing, and of Yahweh, to put his spirit on the one he sends: the anointing is the giving of the spirit and the commission.

evidence.note: “Elisha the son of Shaphat … you shall anoint to be prophet in your place.”
“The spirit of the Lord Yahweh is on me, because (יַעַן) Yahweh has anointed me to bring good news to the poor; he has sent me.”
Jesus reads Isa 61:1 in Nazareth (ἔχρισέν με) and says, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your ears” (Luk 4:21).
“Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with holy spirit and with power, who went about doing good … for God was with him.”
With the oil, “the spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day onward”.

senses.definition: Of the altar and of the priest, on the day of their anointing; of David, made king.

evidence.note: “The leaders offered for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed (הִמָּשַׁח).”
The offering of Aaron and his sons “on the day when he is anointed”.
“The Philistines heard that David had been anointed (נִמְשַׁח) king over all Israel.”

evidence.locator: 1Sa.16.13, וַיִּמְשַׁח → ἔχρισεν; Psa.45.8; Isa.61.1, מְשָׁחֲךָ / מָשַׁח → ἔχρισεν; χρίω renders מָשַׁח ×35

evidence.note: Isa 61:1 quoted: “he anointed (ἔχρισέν) me to preach good news to the poor”.
Psa 45:8 quoted of the Son: “God, your God, anointed (ἔχρισέν) you.”
“Your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed (ἔχρισας)”, after Psa 2:2 (Act 4:26).
“He who establishes us with you into Christ and anointed (χρίσας) us is God.”

parallels.note: “Consecrate”: the piel beside the anointing of the tabernacle and the priests; to anoint is to make holy.
“Pour”: the oil is poured on the head of the one anointed.

words.gloss: anointed; the anointed one (of Yahweh), Messiah
words.summary: The passive form of the verb, “anointed”, used once of a shield and otherwise of a man: the anointed priest in Leviticus, and from Hannah's song on the king, “the anointed of Yahweh”, the man whom no one may touch. It is used of men never anointed with oil (Cyrus, the patriarchs), so that it names the one Yahweh has chosen and set apart. Psa 2 and Dan 9 speak of the anointed one to come; the New Testament gives the word in Greek letters, Μεσσίας, and translates it Χριστός (Jhn 1:41).

senses.definition: As an adjective, rubbed with oil.

evidence.note: David's lament: “There the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, not anointed with oil (בְּלִי מָשִׁיחַ בַּשָּׁמֶן).”

senses.definition: The high priest, הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ, anointed in his father's place, whose sin brings guilt on the people.

evidence.note: “If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people.”
“The priest who is anointed in his place from among his sons shall offer it.”

senses.gloss: the anointed of Yahweh: the king
senses.definition: The king whom Yahweh has chosen and had anointed: Saul and above all David and his line, whom Yahweh saves and upholds, and against whom no one may lift his hand.

evidence.note: David of Saul: “Far be it from me before Yahweh to do this thing to my master, the anointed of Yahweh, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of Yahweh.”
“Who can stretch out his hand against the anointed of Yahweh and be guiltless?”
“How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy the anointed of Yahweh?”
Shimei “cursed the anointed of Yahweh”.
Samuel: “Testify against me before Yahweh and before his anointed.”
Seeing Eliab, Samuel thought, “Surely his anointed is before Yahweh.”
“The oracle of David son of Jesse, the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob.”
“Great salvation he gives to his king (מַלְכּוֹ), and shows steadfast love to his anointed (לִמְשִׁיחוֹ), to David and his seed for ever.”
“Now I know that Yahweh saves his anointed.”
“He is the saving refuge of his anointed.”
“Behold our shield, O God, and look on the face of your anointed.”
“You have been angry with your anointed.”
“For the sake of David your servant, do not turn away the face of your anointed.”
“There I will make a horn sprout for David; I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.”
“The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was caught in their pits”: the last king of Judah.
“You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed.”

senses.gloss: one chosen and commissioned by Yahweh (without oil)
senses.definition: Of men never said to be anointed with oil: Cyrus, whom Yahweh raised up to rebuild Jerusalem, and the patriarchs; “anointed” here is chosen and set apart by Yahweh for his purpose.

evidence.note: “Thus says Yahweh to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him.”
Of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob wandering among the nations: “Do not touch my anointed ones (בִמְשִׁיחָי), and do my prophets no harm.”

senses.gloss: the anointed one to come: Messiah, Christ
senses.definition: The king whom Yahweh will set on Zion against the rebellion of the nations, the anointed ruler of Daniel's seventy sevens who is cut off; in the New Testament, Jesus.

evidence.note: “The kings of the earth set themselves … against Yahweh and against his anointed”; he is Yahweh's king on Zion and his son (Psa 2:6–7).
Psa 2:2 quoted, and applied: “against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate” (Act 4:27).
Hannah, before Israel had a king: “He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.”
“I will raise up for myself a faithful priest … and he shall walk before my anointed for ever.”
“From the going out of the word to restore and build Jerusalem to an anointed one, a ruler (מָשִׁיחַ נָגִיד), seven sevens and sixty-two sevens.”
“After the sixty-two sevens an anointed one shall be cut off (יִכָּרֵת מָשִׁיחַ), and shall have nothing; and the people of the ruler who is to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary.”
Andrew: “We have found the Μεσσίαν, which is translated Christ.”
“I know that Messiah is coming, who is called Christ”; Jesus answers, “I who speak to you am he” (Jhn 4:26).
Simeon would not see death “before he had seen the Lord's anointed (τὸν χριστὸν κυρίου)”.
“God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”

evidence.locator: Lev.4.5, הַמָּשִׁיחַ → χριστός; 1Sa.24.7; Psa.105.15; Isa.45.1 → χριστῷ; Χριστός renders מָשִׁיחַ ×24

evidence.note: “Messiah, which is translated (μεθερμηνευόμενον) Christ”: John gives Χριστός as the Greek for the Hebrew word.
Psa 2:2: “against the Lord and against his Christ (τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ)”.
Peter: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
“It was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and this Jesus … is the Christ.”

evidence.locator: s.v. Μεσσίας
evidence.note: “Aram. מְשִׁיחָא = Heb. מָשִׁיחַ = Χριστός”: Messiah, at Jhn 1:41 and 4:25 only.
“We have found the Messiah (τὸν Μεσσίαν), which is translated Christ.”
The Samaritan woman: “I know that Messiah (Μεσσίας) is coming, who is called Christ; when he comes he will tell us all things.”

parallels.note: “King”: “his king” and “his anointed” stand in parallel.
“Prophet”: “my anointed ones … my prophets” of the patriarchs.
“People”: the salvation of the people and of the anointed together.

words.gloss: anointing; anointing oil; the portion due from the anointing
words.summary: Above all in שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה, the holy anointing oil compounded by Moses' formula, which might not be poured on any other man's flesh or copied (Exo 30:31–33). Also the anointing itself, which made the priesthood Aaron's for ever, and, twice, the priests' portion of the offerings, “given them on the day he anointed them” (Lev 7:35–36).

senses.definition: In שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה: the holy oil of myrrh, cinnamon, cane, cassia and olive oil, by which the tabernacle and the priests were anointed, and which was not for common use.

evidence.note: “You shall make it a holy anointing oil (שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹדֶשׁ), a blend compounded by the perfumer.”
“This shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations”; it is not to be poured on a man's flesh nor made by its formula for anyone else (Exo 30:32).
Blood from the altar and the anointing oil sprinkled on Aaron and his garments, “and he shall be holy”.
“Do not go out from the entrance of the tent of meeting, lest you die, for the anointing oil of Yahweh is upon you.”
The high priest “on whose head the anointing oil was poured”.
“The consecration (נֵזֶר) of the anointing oil of his God is on him.”

senses.gloss: anointing (the act, and the office it confers)
senses.definition: The anointing of Aaron's sons, which made the priesthood theirs, and the garments in which each high priest after him was anointed.

evidence.note: “Their anointing (מָשְׁחָתָם) shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”
“The holy garments of Aaron shall be his sons' after him, to be anointed in them and to fill their hand in them.”

senses.gloss: the priests' portion, due from their anointing
senses.definition: The share of the offerings that belongs to Aaron and his sons, which Yahweh commanded to be given them from the day he anointed them.

evidence.note: “This is the מִשְׁחַת of Aaron and the מִשְׁחַת of his sons from the offerings of Yahweh, on the day he presented them to serve as priests.”
“Which Yahweh commanded to be given them by the sons of Israel on the day he anointed them (בְּיוֹם מָשְׁחוֹ אֹתָם), a statute for ever”: the portion is tied to the anointing.

evidence.locator: Exo.29.7, הַמִּשְׁחָה → χρίσματος; Exo.30.25 → χρῖσμα

evidence.note: “You have an anointing (χρῖσμα) from the Holy One, and you know all things.”
“The anointing which you received from him abides in you … his anointing teaches you about all things.”

words.summary: Once, of the holy gifts given to Aaron and his sons. The brief's 28 tokens under this key are the tokens of מִשְׁחָה, filed together by spelling; the word itself is Num 18:8. Scripture ties the portion to the anointing (Lev 7:35–36); no cognate of the root means “portion” as such.

senses.definition: The share of the holy gifts that Yahweh gives to the priests as theirs for ever.

evidence.note: “I have given you charge of my contributions, all the holy things of the sons of Israel; to you I have given them לְמָשְׁחָה, and to your sons, as a statute for ever.”

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic, twice, in the Persian kings' grants for the house of God: the oil with the wheat, wine and salt. The Hebrew uses שֶׁמֶן for this; the Aramaic names oil by the root of anointing, as the Peshitta's ܡܫܚܐ does.

senses.definition: Olive oil as a staple and an offering.

evidence.note: Darius: “wheat, salt, wine and oil (וּמְשַׁח), as the priests in Jerusalem require”.
Artaxerxes: “up to a hundred baths of oil”.

words.summary: Once, in the lament over the king of Tyre: “a cherub of מִמְשַׁח, the one covering”. Read with the root's common sense it is “anointing”, a cherub anointed, set apart as the tabernacle's things were; the form, a מ-noun, is otherwise unknown, and its tie to the root rests on this one verse.

senses.definition: Said of the king of Tyre, a man (Ezk 28:2, 9), pictured as the anointed covering cherub in the garden of God, cast out for his pride and trade.

evidence.note: “You were a cherub of anointing (כְּרוּב מִמְשַׁח), the one covering; I set you; you were on the holy mountain of God.”
“Take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre.”
“You are a man and not God (אָדָם וְלֹא־אֵל), though you set your heart as the heart of God.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܫܚ (mšaḥ), where the Greek has χρίω and ἀλείφω: the anointing of the head and of the sick with oil, of Jesus' feet and body, and God's anointing of Jesus and of believers.

senses.definition: To rub or pour oil on the head or body: in fasting, in healing the sick, in honour of a guest, and for burial.

evidence.note: “When you fast, anoint your head and wash your face.”
The twelve “anointed with oil (בּמֵשחָא) many who were sick, and healed them”.
“You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment.”
The women bought spices “that they might come and anoint him”.

senses.definition: Of God anointing Jesus with holy spirit and power, and anointing believers.

evidence.note: “God, who has established us with you in the Messiah, and has anointed us.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܫܝܚܐ, about 580 times, where the Greek has both Χριστός and Μεσσίας: it does not need to translate Andrew's word (Jhn 1:41), since it is its own.

senses.definition: The anointed one, the Son of God, of David's seed, who was to suffer and rise; Jesus.

evidence.note: “We have found the Messiah (מְשִׁיחָא).”
“You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
“Has not the scripture said that the Messiah comes from the seed of David?”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܫܝܚܘܬܐ, for χρῖσμα in 1 John.

senses.definition: The anointing believers have received from God, which teaches them.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܫܚܐ, for ἔλαιον: oil for lamps, healing and anointing, and a good of trade.

senses.definition: Olive oil, for lamps, wounds, anointing, and sale.

evidence.note: The foolish virgins “took no oil with them”.
The Samaritan poured on “wine and oil”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's second ܡܫܚ (mšaḥ), for μετρέω in Revelation: to measure the temple and the city. Same spelling as “anoint”; Jewish Aramaic and Arabic have both verbs too. Whether the two are one root is not shown (see the entry's note).

senses.definition: To measure a building or a city with a measuring reed.

evidence.note: “Rise and measure the temple of God and the altar, and those who worship in it.”
“The court outside the temple leave out, and do not measure it.”
“He measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand stadia.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܫܘܚܬܐ, for μέτρον: a measure, and above all the measure God allots to each, of faith, of grace, of the gift of the Messiah.

senses.definition: A measure of length, and the measure or share God deals out to each.

evidence.note: “As God has dealt to each a measure of faith.”
“To each of us grace was given according to the measure of the gift of the Messiah.”
“Within the measure of the boundary which God allotted to us.”
“Fill up the measure of your fathers.”
“By the measure of a man, that is, of an angel.”

cognates.gloss: wipe or stroke with the hand; anoint with oil; (masīḥ) anointed, wiped over with oil
cognates.note: The passing of the hand over a thing is the Hebrew's smearing and rubbing on, and Arabic, like Hebrew, uses it of anointing with oil. Arabic shows ḥ behind ח and s, the regular Arabic answer to Hebrew š, behind ש. The same Arabic verb also means “measure land”, a sense the Peshitta's ܡܫܚ has too (see the note).

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2713, art. مسح, مَسَحَ شَيْئًا (n38555)
evidence.note: “He wiped a thing that was wet or dirty, with his hand, or passed his hand over it … He anointed him or it with oil.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2714, art. مسح, مَسِيحٌ (n38564)
evidence.note: “Anointed: wiped over with some such thing as oil … A king.”

evidence.locator: *mšḥ “anoint”
evidence.note: Sets Arabic masaḥa beside Hebrew, Aramaic, Ugaritic and Punic mšḥ and Akkadian muššuʾu.

cognates.note: As the title of Jesus, the Arabic lexicographers held the word to be taken over from the Hebrew (originally with š); it is a loan out of Hebrew or Aramaic, not evidence for the Hebrew sense.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2714, art. مسح, مَسِيحٌ (n38564)
evidence.note: “المَسِيحُ [The Messiah, the Christ, the Anointed,] Jesus … an arabicized word, [from the Hebrew,] originally مَشِيحَا, with ش.”

cognates.gloss: anoint; anointed, the Messiah; oil, fat
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the verb as the Hebrew's (Targ. Onkelos at Gen 31:13), the passive מְשִׁיחָא of the anointed high priest and, with מַלְכָּא, of the expected king Messiah, and מִשְׁחָא as the common word for oil.

evidence.locator: s.v. מְשַׁח (ch.), citing Targ. O. Gen. XXXI, 13; Targ. II Sam. I, 21 (part. pass. מְשִׁיחַ); Targ. Am. VI, 6 (Ithpe., be rubbed with oil)
s.v. מְשִׁיחָא I, citing Targ. I Sam. XXIV, 7; Targ. I Chr. III, 24 (מַלְכָּא מְשִׁיחָא, the Messiah)
s.v. מִשְׁחָא I, “oil, fat”, citing Targ. Ex. XXIX, 7; Targ. Num. VII, 13

cognates.note: A second Jewish Aramaic verb of the same spelling, “measure”, with מִשְׁחָא “measure, length” (חוּט מִשְׁחָא “measuring line”); the Peshitta has it too (its ܡܫܚ “measure” and ܡܫܘܚܬܐ are words of this entry). Arabic masaḥa also has both senses. Whether the Hebrew מִשְׁחָה / מָשְׁחָה “portion” belongs here is an open question (see the note); it is not named on that sense.

evidence.locator: s.v. מְשַׁח II, citing Targ. Y. Gen. X, 25; Targ. Ez. XL, 5; B. Mets. 107b (do not measure, survey)
s.v. מִשְׁחָא II, “measure, length”, citing Targ. II Chr. IV, 2

cognates.gloss: measure land; mensuration; a measurer of land
cognates.note: In the same Arabic article as “wipe, anoint”, marked by the lexicographers as a figurative use; Jewish Aramaic and the Peshitta also have “measure” beside “anoint” in this spelling.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2713, art. مسح, مَسَحَ شَيْئًا (n38555), A2
evidence.note: “مَسَحَ, inf. n. مَسْحٌ and مِسَاحَةٌ, (tropical:) He measured land.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2714, art. مسح, مِسَاحَةٌ (n38565); مَسَّاحٌ (n38567)
evidence.note: “Mensuration of land”; “a measurer of land”.

cognates.note: Akkadian lost ḥ, which leaves a glottal stop: mšʾ answers to mšḥ. The sense, rubbing on, is the Hebrew's smearing.

evidence.locator: muššuʾu [rub] V (armep x000052860)

evidence.note: “(adj. pergr.) unctus: epitheton honorificum regum Israeliticorum … 2) Messias, Christus (Ps. 2, 2)”.

doctrine.statement: Oil was poured on the head of Aaron and of the kings, “to consecrate him” (Lev 8:12), and the anointing was Yahweh's own act: “has not Yahweh anointed you ruler over his inheritance?” (1Sa 10:1); “I anointed you king over Israel” (2Sa 12:7). With David's anointing “the spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day onward” (1Sa 16:13). The anointed man belonged to Yahweh, so that David would not touch Saul though Saul sought his life: “who can stretch out his hand against the anointed of Yahweh and be guiltless?” (1Sa 24:7; 26:9). Yahweh calls men his anointed who were never anointed with oil, Cyrus (Isa 45:1) and the patriarchs, “do not touch my anointed ones” (Psa 105:15). From the verses: to be anointed is to be chosen by Yahweh and set apart to his service, with his spirit given for the work; the oil was the sign, and the choosing was his.

“We have found the Messiah, which is translated Christ” (Jhn 1:41): Jesus is the מָשִׁיחַ. Jesus read “the spirit of the Lord Yahweh is upon me, because Yahweh has anointed me” and said, “today this scripture is fulfilled” (Isa 61:1; Luk 4:18, 21), and Peter tells “how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with holy spirit and with power … for God was with him” (Act 10:38). The anointing was God's gift to a man: “God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions”, because “you love righteousness and hate wickedness” (Psa 45:8; Heb 1:9); the anointed one has a God, and companions above whom he is set. He is the anointed king of Psa 2, set on Zion, to whom Yahweh says “you are my son; today I have begotten you” (Psa 2:2, 6–7), words Paul reads of the resurrection (Act 13:33); Peter confesses him “the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Mat 16:16), and “God has made him both Lord and Christ” (Act 2:36). The Christ is “of the seed of David” (Jhn 7:42), as Yahweh shows steadfast love “to his anointed, to David and his seed for ever” (Psa 18:51). From the verses: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, begotten by God, anointed by God with his spirit (his power) and made Lord and Christ by him; he is the man God chose, not God himself, and not one who existed before his birth.

In Psa 2 the kings of the earth set themselves “against Yahweh and against his anointed”, and Yahweh answers, “I have set my king on Zion, my holy hill”, and gives him the nations as his inheritance and the ends of the earth as his possession, to break them with a rod of iron (Psa 2:2, 6, 8–9). The apostles read the first part as fulfilled when Herod and Pilate gathered “against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed” (Act 4:26–27), and Revelation the last part, when “the kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign for ever and ever” (Rev 11:15; 12:5). Hannah's song, “Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed” (1Sa 2:10), is in the same terms. From the verses: the anointed one, rejected by the rulers at his first coming, will reign on earth from Zion over the nations, as Yahweh's king.

Daniel is told that seventy sevens are decreed “to finish transgression, to make an end of sins, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness … and to anoint a holy of holies” (Dan 9:24); from the word to restore and build Jerusalem “to an anointed one, a ruler” is seven sevens and sixty-two sevens, and “after the sixty-two sevens an anointed one shall be cut off and shall have nothing; and the people of the ruler who is to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; its end shall be with a flood” (Dan 9:25–26). Isaiah says of the servant, “he was cut off from the land of the living; for the transgression of my people he was stricken” (Isa 53:8). Jesus foretold of the temple, “there shall not be left here one stone upon another” (Mat 24:2), pointed to “the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet” (Mat 24:15), and said, “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near” (Luk 21:20). From the verses: the anointed one cut off is Jesus in his death for the sins of his people, and the destruction of the city and sanctuary that follows was the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and the temple in AD 70.

Paul writes, “he who establishes us with you into Christ (εἰς Χριστόν) and anointed us is God” (2Co 1:21), and John, “you have an anointing from the Holy One … the anointing which you received from him abides in you” (1Jn 2:20, 27). Those who are the anointed one's are anointed in him, as the patriarchs were Yahweh's anointed ones (Psa 105:15), and “if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise” (Gal 3:29). From the verses: the believer shares in the anointing of the Christ, chosen by God and set apart, and with him an heir of the promise made to Abraham.

The “cherub of anointing, the one covering” is addressed in a lament over “the king of Tyre” (Ezk 28:12, 14), and the same chapter tells the prince of Tyre, “you are a man and not God”, who will die “the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers” (Ezk 28:2, 9–10). His sin is named: “by the abundance of your trade you were filled with violence … your heart was lifted up because of your beauty” (Ezk 28:16–17). From the verses: the anointed cherub is a human king, pictured in the garden of God and the tabernacle's covering cherub; the passage is not about a fallen angel.

note: Left out: מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל (m.dt.al), filed here by BDB but formed from Aramaic שׁיזב “deliver” and אֵל, not this root; it belongs to a שׁיזב entry, and no name file is made here. מֶשִׁי “silk” (m.dt.aj, Ezk 16:10, 13) has no ח and is not formed from this root (its origin is unknown; Jastrow's Aramaic מְשֵׁי “rub, wash” is a lead for a משׁי root); left for its own entry. Isa 52:14 מִשְׁחַת, which the brief counts under מִשְׁחָה by spelling, is “marring” from שׁחת and is already in shachat (מִשְׁחַת, v.cq.ad). The zero-token key m.ck.aq (מִמְשַׁח, “see משׁח”) is a cross-reference and is not given. The keys m.dt.ab and m.dt.ac share their 28 tokens because the brief groups by spelling: מָשְׁחָה itself is Num 18:8 (perhaps Lev 7:35 too). Open questions: (1) whether the “portion” of Lev 7:35 and Num 18:8 is the portion due from the anointing (Lev 7:36 ties it so, and that is how it is written) or a second root “measure”, attested in Jewish Aramaic מְשַׁח II, Arabic masaḥa “measure land”, the Peshitta's ܡܫܚ “measure” (Rev 11:1; 21:15–17) and ܡܫܘܚܬܐ “measure” (Rom 12:3; Eph 4:7, 13, 16; 2Co 10:13), and Akkadian mašāḫu “measure” (not checked in CAD; its ḫ would make it a different root from the Arabic ḥ). The Peshitta measure words are entered as their own syc words, with the Aramaic and Arabic “measure” cognates. (2) Ugaritic mšḥ: check DULAT's article and KTU 1.10 II for the reading before naming it on the verb. (3) Punic mšḥ “anoint” (Anderson–Moser) not yet checked in Krahmalkov. (4) Ezk 28:14 מִמְשַׁח: “anointing” rests on the root's common sense; an alternative ties it to “measure, extend”.
